deities: Chandi Devi (Chandika, a fierce form of Parvati/Shakti)

history.dynasty: Suchat Singh, King of Kashmir (present structure, 1929); idol traditionally installed by Adi Shankaracharya (8th century)
history.summary: Chandi Devi Temple crowns Neel Parvat, the eastern summit of the Sivalik Hills overlooking Haridwar, and is also known as Neel Parvat Teerth, one of the Panch Tirth (Five Pilgrimages) of Haridwar. Legend holds that after Goddess Chandika slew the demon kings Shumbha and Nishumbha (and their commanders Chanda and Munda, from whom she takes the name Chamunda), she rested on this hilltop; the two nearby peaks are said to be named Shumbha and Nishumbha. The main idol is traditionally believed to have been installed by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century, while the present temple structure was built in 1929 by Suchat Singh, King of Kashmir. It is one of the three Siddh Peeths of Haridwar (with Mansa Devi and Maya Devi) where wishes are believed to be fulfilled. The summit is reached by the Chandi Devi Udankhatola ropeway from the base near Chandighat (5-10 minutes) or a 3-4 km forest trek.

name: Chandi Devi Temple
town_description: Haridwar, in the Haridwar district of Uttarakhand at the foothills of the Sivalik Hills where the Ganga enters the plains, is one of Hinduism's seven holy cities (Sapta Puri) and one of the four Kumbh Mela sites. Its spiritual heart is Har Ki Pauri, where the evening Ganga Aarti draws thousands daily. Mansa Devi and Chandi Devi temples crown the twin hills (Bilwa Parvat and Neel Parvat) overlooking the city, while the Maya Devi temple sits near Birla Ghat and Daksheshwar Mahadev lies in the adjoining heritage township of Kankhal.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 40 km; 70-80 min by taxi).
travel.railway: Haridwar Junction (approx. 4-8 km; autos, e-rickshaws and cabs to the ropeway base at Chandighat).
travel.road: The Chandi Devi Udankhatola ropeway base is near Chandighat, approx. 4 km from Har Ki Pauri; ropeway hours roughly 7:00 AM-6:00 PM, tickets approx. Rs. 150 one-way / Rs. 250 round-trip (combo with Mansa Devi approx. Rs. 400-500). A 3 km uphill trek (45-60 minutes) is the alternative.

visitor_information.best_time: February to June and September to November; October-March is the most comfortable season. Chandi Chaudas and Navratri draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opening hours conflict across sources (verify): commonly 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM with a midday closure 12:00-3:00 PM, or 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 3:00-6:00 PM, or 5:00 AM-7:00 PM. Ropeway roughly 7:00 AM-6:00 PM (seasonal). No temple entry fee; photography inside is not allowed.
